sentences.text: Shri Khalid Noor Fakhruddin, learned counsel for the ap  Ms. Shikha Sharma, learned Government   respondent/State.
Heard on I.A.No.21295/2025, which is first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C., for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant-Dinesh.

Appellant - Dinesh , is aggrieved of the judgment dated 10.06.2024, passed by the learned Additional Session Judge, Junnardeo, District Chhindwara (M.P.), in Special Case No.01/2023,
whereby, appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under :-
 Conviction Sen  
 Section Act Imprisonment Fi  
 4(2) POCSO R.I. for life Rs.2,
 5(L)/6 POCSO R.I. for life Rs.2,
 363 IPC R.I. for 5 years Rs.2,
 366A IPC R.I. for 5 years Rs.2,
 376(2)(N) IPC Nil Nil   376(3) IPC Nil Nil  Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that in view of Ex.P/14(c), which is a dhakil kharij register, wherein victim had taken admission on 2 CRA-10317-2024 06/07/2017 in 4th class, is available on record.
In this document, it is mentioned that date of birth was recorded on the basis of transfer certificate.
Prosecution has not produced first class school admission register.
Onus was on prosecution to produce and prove first class school admission register.
Evidence of the lady doctor PW/11 reveals that victim's secondary sexual characters were fully developed.
Victim admits that she was a consenting adult and performed marriage with the appellant.
She was pregnant with appellant and carried 8 months pregnancy.
Hence, prayer is made to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and release him on bail.

sentences.text: Ms. Shikha Sharma, learned Government Advocate for the State opposes the prayer of the appellant.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case to suspend the remaining part of the jail sentence of the present appellant and to release him on bail.

Taking all the facts into consideration and largely failure of the prosecution to produce first entry register and also the TC on the basis of which, so called date of birth was recorded, balance appears to tilt in favour of the appellant, without commencing on merits of the case, it is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only), with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court 3 CRA-10317-2024 for his appearance before the Trial Court on 23.04.2026 and such other dates as may be fixed by the Trial Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence imposed upon Appellant - Dinesh shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
I.A.No. 21295/2025, is allowed & disposed of.
